sources.entry: Schliff by Zandereins - Deterministic quality scorer for AI agent instruction files — 8-dimension scoring with security, multi-format (SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, AGENTS.md), anti-gaming detection, zero dependencies

summary.one_liner: Schliff is a deterministic, rule-based quality scorer (0–100 with letter grades) for AI agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, and system prompts, with no LLM judge in the scoring path.
summary.what_it_does: Scores instruction files against a versioned rubric using a set of readable scorers (structure, triggers, quality, edges, efficiency, composability, clarity, security), combined into a weighted composite. The AGENTS.md headline uses structure, operational_coverage, and efficiency, while other formats use the 7-dimension composite, which needs an eval suite for some dimensions. Unmeasured dimensions count as zero, so coverage gaps lower the score ceiling. It offers CLI commands for scoring, CI gating with a minimum score, checking that referenced commands exist, badge generation, diffing and comparing scores across commits, ranking fixes, and generating reports. An optional improvement loop (evolve) applies rule-based patches and re-scores, keeping changes only if the score improves. Core scoring is stdlib-only and makes no network calls.
use_cases: grade the quality of an AGENTS.md file
gate pull requests on instruction-file quality in CI
lint SKILL.md or CLAUDE.md files before committing
compare instruction file scores across git commits
find token-budget bloat in agent instruction files
generate a score badge for a repository's agent config
notable: Deterministic scoring: same input gives the same score, with no LLM judge and no randomness
Full-denominator composite: unmeasured dimensions count as zero, so the score ceiling reflects measurement coverage
Multi-format support for AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, and system prompts
Anti-gaming checks that discount padding, repeated lines, keyword stuffing, and junk commands
Claude Code plugin exposing /schliff: commands alongside the CLI
caveats: Optional LLM extras (evolve, judge) send requests to a provider using the user's own API key; core scoring makes no network calls
The README says the rubric measures measurable properties, not whether the file's content is actually correct; a plausible but false file can still score well
Some dimensions require an eval suite (generated with /schliff:init) before the full composite can be scored
